newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-OLD PALS DALGLISH AND SOUNESS END ALL SQUARE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-OLD PALS DALGLISH AND SOUNESS END ALL SQUARE.

text.p: There were countless photos -- they called them "Jock pictures" -- of Kenny Dalglish, Graeme Souness and Alan Hansen grinning in delight together celebrating another Liverpool trophy back in the 1970s and 80s.

As Dalglish describes in his autobiography published last year, the three Scots who contributed so much to Liverpool's domination of the English game, always posed together after they had won another bauble.
"We had a tradition called Jock Picture. Every time Liverpool won a trophy the three of us would run around shouting 'Jock Picture, Jock Picture," says Dalglish.

"I've got all these pictures of the three of us jumping up and down with yet another cup at Wembley. Terry Mac (McDermott) tried to sneak in, but we wouldn't have it. It was an exclusive club, only for Jocks."
McDermott and Dalglish were certainly photographed together on Saturday when the three old Liverpool team mates all met up at the Dell.

No longer wearing the red shirts of Liverpool, Dalglish and McDermott were in Newcastle's black-and-white striped corner while Souness, now the manager of Southampton and the man who succeeded Dalglish as Liverpool manager in 1991, was in the red-and-white striped one.

And the pictures of the three at the end of Saturday's English premier league game would have told quite a story after Southampton scored twice in the last two minutes to earn a 2-2 draw against a Newcastle side who had looked home and dry.

Dalglish, who was officially in charge of Newcastle for the first time since taking over last Tuesday from Kevin Keegan, another Liverpool old boy, thought his new side were on their way to victory as they led 2-0 with a 14th minute goal from Les Ferdinand and an 82nd minute strike from Lee Clark.

But then suddenly, the Saints were alive again. With two minutes to play Neil Maddison took advantage of a mistake by goalkeeper Shaka Hislop to score and with the referee looking at his watch, Matt Le Tissier blasted home an unstoppable drive from 25 metres with the last kick of the game to give Southampton a point.
"You can't do anything about a goal like that, he's hit one out of his socks," said Dalglish afterwards.
He added: "It was good to be back, but although we didn't win I am proud of the way the team played."

Souness had sent his old pal a good luck message when he took over at Newcastle, but also said this was the worst time to be playing Southampton as they would be so desperate to do well. He was spot on.

Impressed with his side's grit and determination, Souness also praised Le Tissier after leaving him out of the starting lineup that beat Middlesbrough last week. Earlier he had laughed off reports that he and Le Tissier had had any sort of falling-out. He said: "You can't believe everything you read in the newspapers."
Dalglish and Souness didn't stop to pose for pictures

afterwards, but did share a laugh as they walked back to the dressing room, overcoats done up against the cold, reflecting on another shared football match, but this time from very different perspectives.
